thought.text: Let me verify the Vite API proxy forwarding and overall compose health.

reasoning_content:
The frontend uses env vars at build time (`import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL`) since the placeholders start with `__` and are ignored at runtime. Fine.

Let me verify the frontend proxy actually forwards to backend services. Test an API path through vite proxy: `http://localhost:3002/pls/v1/...` or openapi.json. Let me test through the vite proxy on 3002 (bypassing oauth2-proxy) and also check that the proxy is configured.

Test: curl http://localhost:3002/pls/v1/... maybe there's an OpenAPI. Actually the proxy strips prefix. Let's hit `http://localhost:3002/pls/v1/healthz` → forwards to localhost:18000/healthz.

Let me test that. Also test that the frontend serves the app JS bundle.

Let me also verify docker compose health status (all healthy) via docker compose ps.

Let me now do a functional end-to-end check of the workflow as described. That requires an LLM (placeholder) and Docling (not running). The guide says external AI services are not part of the local stack. So can't run full workflow. But the workflow submission should at least start Temporal workflow. That might fail due to LLM. The guide says external services are placeholders (not part of local stack). So E2E workflow isn't expected to complete.

Given the installation summary notes external LLM/Docling are placeholder endpoints — that's consistent with the guide (local stack does not start an LLM provider; you provide external). The summary says "placeholder endpoints (not part of the local stack)".

Let's focus on validating the installation is complete and operational. Key checks:
- Docker infra: 11 running.
- process-compose: 33 running, 5 completed seeds, no failed.
- Keycloak login works, token acquisition works.
- Frontend serves.
- Databases seeded and migrated.
- Backend APIs healthy.
- Temporal, MinIO, Qdrant, SpiceDB running.

Let me check the vite proxy forwarding and docker compose ps. Also verify `uv run poe` tasks and that key python packages are importable.

Let me also confirm the .env has the docker-compose override used (minio legacy images) — this is a workaround, but it's fine, it's an installation method variation. Note the guide says docker.io/minio. The override is a workaround for image availability. This is acceptable.

Let me check the vite proxy and the OpenAPI reachability through frontend.
